extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and practitioners handling inter partes reexamination (patent owners, third-party requesters, and their attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for preparing, issuing, responding to, and processing Office actions in inter partes reexamination proceedings before the USPTO (MPEP §§2660–2666). Focuses on examiner duties, timing, communications, and parties' filing/response obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Office action must respond to third-party arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The first action should respond to the substance of each argument raised in the request by the third party requester pursuant to 37 CFR 1.915. Also, it should address any issues proper for reexamination that the examiner becomes aware of independent of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the first Office action substantively addresses every argument raised by the requester; also independently raise/address any examiner-discovered reexamination issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of third-party materials (claim charts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the request for reexamination includes material such as a claim chart to explain a proposed rejection, the examiner may cut and paste the claim chart (or other material) to incorporate it within the body of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incorporating third-party material, carefully review it to ensure that any items incorporated in a statement of rejection 'clearly and completely address the patentability of the claims.' Do not blindly adopt wording — confirm completeness and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent actions must address prior responses and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: For actions subsequent to the first Office action, the examiner must be careful to additionally address all patent owner responses to previous actions and third party requester comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every subsequent Office action should explicitly consider and respond to earlier patent owner submissions and third-party comments; omissions are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: No patent owner amendment before first Office action (37 CFR 1.939(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, there will be no patent owner amendment to address in the first Office action of the inter partes reexamination, because 37 CFR 1.939(b) prohibits a patent owner amendment prior to first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because amendments are prohibited pre-first action, the first Office action will ordinarily contain no rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 112; 35 U.S.C. 112 rejections are proper in reexamination only when raised by an amendment of the patent, except in merged proceedings where an amendment already exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution patent owner about ACP and strict enforcement of post-ACP rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of the requirement for 'special dispatch' in inter partes reexamination proceedings (35 U.S.C. 314(c)), the first action should include a statement cautioning the patent owner that a complete response should be made to the action, since the next action is expected to be an ACP. The first action should further caution the patent owner that the requirements of 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced after an ACP and that any amendment after the ACP must include 'a showing of good and sufficient reasons why they are necessary and were not earlier presented' in order to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert form paragraph 26.05 at the end of the first Office action followed by form paragraph 26.73 to warn patent owner about limited opportunities after the ACP and the need for thorough early submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers to be submitted in response to this Office action (¶ 26.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to ensure full consideration of any amendments, affidavits or declarations, or other documents as evidence of patentability, such documents must be submitted in response to this Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions after the next Office action (intended to be an ACP) will be governed by 37 CFR 1.116(b) and (d), which will be strictly enforced; file affidavits/declarations/amendments promptly in direct response to the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence handling and contact information (¶ 26.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence relating to this inter partes reexamination proceeding should be directed to the Central Reexamination Unit (mail/fax/hand addresses provided). Any inquiry concerning this communication or earlier communications from the examiner, or as to the status of this proceeding, should be directed to the Central Reexamination Unit at the listed telephone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified CRU addresses and phone/fax numbers; follow mailing/transmittal procedures in Office action instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action cover sheet and signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office action cover sheet is PTOL-2064. Where the Office action is a first Office action, the space on the PTOL-2064 for the date of the communication to which the Office action is responsive should not be filled in. As with all other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding, the first Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not fill in 'responsive to' date for first OA; ensure primary examiner signs the first OA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference before issuing Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: After an examiner has determined that the reexamination proceeding is ready for an Office action, the examiner will formulate a draft preliminary Office action and inform the CRU SPE or TC QAS of intent to issue it. The CRU SPE/TC QAS will convene a panel review conference, and the conference members will review the patentability of the claim(s) pursuant to MPEP § 2671.03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conference confirms the examiner’s preliminary decision to reject and/or allow the claims, the proposed Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner with two other conferees initialing. If not confirmed, the examiner must reevaluate and issue an appropriate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt or explain rejections and provide statutory basis and reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions must set forth rejections with statutory citations (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 103) and explain the factual/technical reasoning (e.g., how references combine to render claims unpatentable). Proposed third-party rejections may be adopted essentially as proposed where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear explanation of how prior art references teach claim limitations and why combination would have been obvious; expressly note when a rejection was proposed by a third party and whether adopted or rejected, with reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: do not consider issues outside reexamination (37 CFR 1.906(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues not within the scope of reexamination proceedings (e.g., certain public use questions) will not be considered in a reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.906(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If third-party raises out-of-scope issues, note they are outside reexamination and advise patent owner of alternative remedies (e.g., consider filing a reissue application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail first Office action with order granting reexamination when possible (special dispatch)
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of 'special dispatch' (35 U.S.C. 314(c)), it is intended that the examiner will issue an ACP at the earliest possible time. Accordingly, the first action should include statements cautioning the patent owner that a complete response should be made since the next action is expected to be an ACP. All reexamination proceedings will be 'special' throughout their pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to mail the examiner’s first Office action on the merits ordinarily together with the order granting reexamination; prioritize reexamination files, especially those involved in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing timing and handoff after draft prepared
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner will prepare the action, ensure clerical processing, and forward the reexamination to the CRU SPE no later than two (2) weeks from the date of the consultation conference. The action is reviewed by the CRU SPE, who then hand carries the action to the Reexamination Legal Advisor (RLA) within three (3) days of the CRU SPE’s receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet the two-week and three-day internal handoff timings to support special dispatch and timely mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title change procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, the title of the patent will not need to be changed during reexamination. Where a change is necessary, the examiner should point it out early in prosecution as part of an Office action. A change in the title in a reexamination can only be effected via a formal examiner’s amendment accompanying the NIRC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing the title by merely initialing is not permitted. The examiner’s decision on title change is final and not subject to review; notify patent owner early to permit comment before NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dependent claims when base claim rejected/canceled
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unamended base patent claim has been rejected or canceled, any claim which is directly or indirectly dependent thereon should be indicated as patentable if it is otherwise patentable. No requirement should be made for rewriting the dependent claim in independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reject or object to dependent claims solely because their base claim was canceled, except in specified situations: if a new base claim has been canceled, a dependent claim depending thereon should be rejected as indefinite; if an amended/new base claim is rejected, dependent claims should be objected to if otherwise patentable and require rewriting in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority and special status rules (35 U.S.C. 314(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: All inter partes reexamination proceedings shall be conducted with special dispatch. Cases involved in litigation have priority over all other cases; reexaminations not involved in litigation have priority over other cases except those involved in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give reexaminations expedited handling consistent with statutory special dispatch; apply priority rules when scheduling and allocating resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response and comments timing (general schedule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods for response and comments are defined for various stages: (A) After a non-ACP Office action: patent owner normally 2 months; third party may once file comments within 30 days of service. (B) After Office letter indicating patent owner response not proper: patent owner must complete response within time set (normally 30 days or one month); third party comments within 30 days of service. (C) After an ACP: patent owner may once file comments and/or a proposed amendment within the time set (normally 30 days or one month); third party may once file comments within 30 days from service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the single-opportunity filing limits (e.g., third-party may file comments only once after patent owner response), the specified time periods, and the shorter deadlines in litigation-related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and cross-appeal timing (non-extendable)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a Right of Appeal Notice, the patent owner and the third party requester may each file a notice of appeal within 30 days or one month (whichever is longer). The time for filing a notice of appeal cannot be extended. Cross-appeals may be filed within fourteen days of service under limited conditions. Times for filing briefs, rebuttals, and requests for oral hearing are set and generally non-extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strictly enforce non-extendable appeal/cross-appeal and brief filing deadlines (see specified CFR provisions); failure to meet deadlines forecloses rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefs, rebuttal briefs, and oral hearing requests timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant briefs and fee within two months after last-filed notice of appeal; respondent brief within one month from service of appellant brief; rebuttal briefs within one month of examiner’s answer; request for oral hearing within two months after examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These times may not be extended; follow 37 CFR 41.66 and 41.73 for filing windows and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing of Office actions and transmittal to third-party requester
rubrics_metrics.description: After an Office action is completed and approved by CRU SPE/TC QAS and the RLA, the action is mailed by CRU support staff. All actions in an inter partes reexamination proceeding will have a copy mailed to the third party requester. A transmittal form PTOL-2070 must be used for each requester and additional partial owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PALM printing for addresses; prepare PTOL-2070 transmittals for each requester and partial owner; number of transmittals indicates number of copies to mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time governed by 37 CFR 1.956 — requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for taking any action by a patent owner in an inter partes reexamination proceeding will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified. Any request for such extension must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due and must be accompanied by the petition set forth in § 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.136(a)/(b) do NOT apply. Extensions are not available to third party requesters. CRU Director decides extension requests; requests considered only after first Office action is mailed. Requests must state what actions patent owner has taken to prepare a response and why additional time is needed; evaluate by balancing fair opportunity vs statutory special dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary grants and limits on extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution will be conducted by initially setting a time period of at least 30 days or one month (whichever is longer). First requests for extensions for sufficient cause will usually be granted for a reasonable time (usually one month). Second or subsequent requests, or requests for more than one month, will be granted only in extraordinary situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual accounting of reasonably diligent behavior to receive favorable consideration; mere filing of request does not effect extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions to submit affidavits after ACP — limited and scrutinized
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request for extension is made to submit an affidavit after an ACP, granting the extension is without prejudice to examiner questioning why the affidavit is now necessary and why it was not earlier presented. If the showing is insufficient, the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit notwithstanding grant of extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits submitted after an ACP are subject to the same treatment as amendments submitted after an ACP; be prepared to justify late affidavits with good reasons why earlier submission was not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner reply requirements (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, the patent owner must reply to the Office action. The reply must be reduced to writing which 'distinctly and specifically points out the supposed errors in the examiner’s action' and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action. The reply must present arguments pointing out the specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over any applied references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies must be a bona fide attempt to advance the proceeding. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specific argument is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies — limited entry as matter of right
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply that is supplemental to a reply in compliance with § 1.111(b) will not be entered as a matter of right except if clearly limited to specified categories (cancellation of claims; adoption of examiner suggestions; placement in condition for allowance; reply to Office requirement made after first reply; correction of informalities; simplification of issues for appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental replies will be entered only when they fall within the enumerated categories or if filed within a period where Office action is suspended under § 1.103(a) or (c). Plan initial replies accordingly to avoid reliance on supplemental entry.
